    How Animator Prep Works

    01

    Upload a Scene

    Upload an illustration, product visual, game scene, or photo with a subject you want to animate independently.

    02

    Separate Visual Layers

    AI identifies the subject and background, producing transparent PNG layers for each.

    03

    Reconstruct Hidden Areas

    AI estimates and fills in the background areas that were hidden behind the subject — so no holes appear when layers move.

    04

    Export for Animation

    Download transparent PNG layers or a layered PSD ready for After Effects, Blender, or any motion graphics tool.

    Accuracy and Limitations

    Best results come from scenes with clearly separated subjects and visible depth.

    Complex occlusions, fine hair edges, or heavily overlapping objects may require manual touch-up after export.

    Animator Prep does not separate internal character parts. For hair, face, clothing, and limbs, continue with Character into Layers.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What layers does Animator Prep create?
    Animator Prep attempts to separate a flat image into scene-level layers such as foreground details, the main subject or complete character, supporting objects, midground elements, and a reconstructed background. The exact number and type of layers depend on the visible composition and the selected layer detail.
    Can I use the result for parallax animation?
    Yes. The separated foreground, subject, midground, and background layers can be moved at different speeds to create simple parallax, camera push-ins, pans, and depth effects. The tool prepares the visual assets but does not automatically create the final animation.
    Does Animator Prep separate hair, face, clothing, and limbs?
    Not by default. Animator Prep focuses on scene-level separation, such as the complete character, props, foreground, and background. For hair, face, eyes, mouth, clothing, limbs, and accessories, use Character into Layers after extracting the complete character from the scene.
    Can it reconstruct the background behind a character or object?
    Yes. AI may generate a visually plausible clean background for areas that were previously covered by the subject. However, it cannot recover the original unseen pixels. Reconstructed areas are AI estimates and should be reviewed before final production use.
    What kinds of images work best?
    The best results usually come from high-resolution images with clear subjects and object boundaries, visible separation between foreground and background, limited motion blur, moderate overlap between elements, and enough visible background around the main subject. Glass, smoke, fine hair, reflections, and heavily overlapping objects may require additional cleanup.
    Can I export the result as PNG layers or a PSD?
    Yes. You can export the separated visual elements as transparent PNG layers or download the complete composition as a layered PSD for continued work in Photoshop, After Effects, or another compatible editor. The PSD contains raster layers, not the image's original source layers.
    Does this create a finished animation?
    No. Animator Prep creates animation-ready visual layers. You still need an animation or compositing application to add keyframes, camera motion, rigging, transitions, and final timing. The generated assets can be used as a starting point in tools such as After Effects, Photoshop, Blender, or other motion software.
    Can I use Animator Prep for character animation?
    Yes, when you need to separate the complete character from the surrounding scene for camera motion, parallax, or simple cutout animation. For detailed character rigging, first extract the complete character with Animator Prep, then send that character layer to Character into Layers for a finer body-part breakdown.
    How many credits does Animator Prep use?
    Animator Prep uses 30 credits per run. Failed processing jobs are refunded according to the platform's credit policy.
